_comment: Hand-authored standardized narrative templates used to seed report-section detail text. Unlike dropdowns.json (regenerated by build/build_data.py from the FWIN ESS Template), this file is durable and safe to edit by hand. Keys are consumed by assets/app.js (sectionNarrative / suggestNote) and mirrored by the ess-collect skill.
impact_boilerplate: The site footprint is small and largely cleared/disturbed, and no critical habitat has been identified within the site boundary. Based on the scale and nature of the proposed works, impacts to these matters are not expected. Field staff should remain alert and report any listed species observed on site.
migratory_note: Listed migratory species are a separate matter of national environmental significance from threatened species. Any recorded in the wider area are typically highly mobile, and a small, disturbed site footprint is unlikely to provide important habitat; no impacts are expected.
acid_sulfate_note: Acid sulfate soils may occur in the area. Manage any ground disturbance and dewatering accordingly and consult the Atlas of Australian Acid Sulfate Soils before works.
duty_of_care: Standard cultural-heritage duty of care applies. If anything of potential cultural significance is uncovered during works, activity must stop and the relevant Traditional Owner group (and the state cultural-heritage body) must be contacted before work resumes.
no_ipa_note: No Indigenous Protected Areas are recorded over the site. Standard cultural-heritage duty of care still applies (see above).
no_heritage_note: No listed World, National, Commonwealth or State heritage places or values were identified at or immediately adjacent to the site.

general_biosecurity_obligation.NSW: Under the Biosecurity Act 2015 (NSW), any person dealing with biosecurity matter or a carrier has a general biosecurity duty to ensure that, so far as is reasonably practicable, any biosecurity risk is prevented, eliminated or minimised. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit and do not move soil, plant material or water that could carry a pest, weed or disease.
general_biosecurity_obligation.VIC: Under the Catchment and Land Protection Act 1994 (Vic), land users must take all reasonable steps to prevent the growth and spread of declared noxious weeds and to control established pest animals. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit to avoid spreading weeds, pests or pathogens.
general_biosecurity_obligation.SA: Under the Landscape South Australia Act 2019, land owners and occupiers have duties to control declared plants and animals. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit to avoid spreading declared pests, weeds or pathogens.
general_biosecurity_obligation.WA: Under the Biosecurity and Agriculture Management Act 2007 (WA), everyone has obligations to prevent the spread of declared pests. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit to avoid spreading declared pests, weeds or pathogens.
general_biosecurity_obligation.TAS: Under the Biosecurity Act 2019 (Tas), a person who deals with biosecurity matter has a general biosecurity duty to take reasonable and practical measures to prevent or minimise each biosecurity risk. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit.
general_biosecurity_obligation.NT: Under NT biosecurity and weed-management legislation, land users must take reasonable steps to prevent the spread of declared weeds and pests. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit.
general_biosecurity_obligation.ACT: Under the Pest Plants and Animals Act 2005 (ACT), land custodians must manage declared pest plants and animals. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit.
general_biosecurity_obligation.*: Personnel have a general obligation to take reasonable and practical steps to prevent the spread of pests, weeds, diseases and contaminants that are within their control. Clean down vehicles, equipment and footwear before and after the site visit, and do not move soil, plant material or water that could carry a pest or pathogen.

koala.explainer: Under the Nature Conservation (Koala) Conservation Plan, Queensland is divided into koala districts A, B and C. Districts A and B cover South East Queensland; the remainder of the State is district C. The sequential clearing requirements in Section 10 of the plan apply only to koala habitat trees in districts A and B.
koala.district_ab: This site falls within South East Queensland, where koala districts A/B apply. The Koala Conservation Plan's sequential clearing requirements may apply to the clearing of koala habitat trees — confirm the district and any assessable-development triggers against the plan and the koala habitat mapping before works.
koala.district_c: This site is in koala district C (outside South East Queensland), so the sequential clearing requirements in Section 10 of the Koala Conservation Plan (which apply only to districts A and B) do not apply here. Koalas may still be present, and general duty of care applies.
koala.confirm: Provisional district from location only — confirm against the official Koala Conservation Plan mapping.
